pr_title: Re-read last imap_email_content email when no change
pr_body:
<!--

## Proposed change
<!-- 
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

In the Bug #35975 it is stated an issue that the state changes to Unknown after some time. This is actually not dependent on time, but on arrival of emails. So basically if no email arrives, the code will not find any unread email at all and default to returning None out of the read_next() method. However, this now is obviously undesired behavior if people decide to keep the emails in the mailbox. 

This basically restores the original intent of staying in the previous state by trying to return the last detected email, if no change of emails occur at all, but supports still the *deleted email* usecase, because in that case email would become None, and state would turn to None again.

I assume that this matches more the initial intent of this piece of code

issue_context.title: imap_email_content set to unknown after 30 seconds
issue_context.body:
## The problem
I know there was a breaking change in 0.110.0, that imap_email_content should be set to unknown, when there is no email found. But the way it works (at least with Gmail) is, that the sensor sets its value correctly after receiving the email, but after 30 seconds it sets its status to an unknown, even then the email still sits in the inbox. So the sensor is basically useless, it has unknown value all the time except for 30 seconds after receiving the email.

## Environment
- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 0.110.0
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): 0.109.0
- Operating environment (Home Assistant/Supervised/Docker/venv):  Ubuntu 19.10/Docker
- Integration causing this issue:  imap_email_content
- Link to integration documentation on our website:  https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/imap_email_content/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
```yaml
sensor:
  - platform: imap_email_content
    name: Alarm
    server: imap.gmail.com
    port: 993
    username: !secret gmail_username
    password: !secret gmail_password
    senders:
      - !secret alarm_email
    value_template: "{{ subject.split('Alarm - ')[1] }}"
```

## Traceback/Error logs
No errors

## Additional information
I am not deleting the emails. They sit in the inbox all the time.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/44951610/82662731-b2c67280-9c2e-11ea-9920-f4f824739f14.png)

This was changed by https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/35123 by @MartinHjelmare
comments:
Hi,

That is a little related to the breaking change:

The two added lines in my PR were explicitly setting the message object to None (leading to unknown) when the message itself has become None (if email_message is None => self._message = None)

The problem is however related to a more generic issue in the sensor implementation; which was hidden before my changes were applied. Before those changes, the last read email was always kept as a sensor value, even if you remove it from imap.

In this case, however, to provide an appropriate fix, I would like to first find out if this block becomes activated - which inherently would lead to a None message:
`
except imaplib.IMAP4.error:

            _LOGGER.info("Connection to %s lost, attempting to reconnect", self._server)
            try:
                self.connect()
            except imaplib.IMAP4.error:
                _LOGGER.error("Failed to reconnect")
`

Because this is the final line of the read_next() method; it will return None

Tbh, in my usecase I had been using incoming emails to trigger other stuff and I cared only switching from and to Unknown; thus sensor becoming Unknown when I deleted the original email, was exactly what I needed and what was missing in the impl. 

However, when looking deeply, it gives the impression that the usecase "not finding any new email at all" is also not so working well...

The other question I have is for the author of the module itself; what is the intention behind the unread-id thing? How should it work? If the email is not deleted, and no new email arrives, should it not return the last email actually? Currently it does not. is this maybe the root cause of this bug? If yes, I can make a PR for that change.

The use case is, that the device sends an email on state change. In my case, alarm armed/disarmed. If it gets armed, it stays armed, until it gets disarmed. State unknown is useless.
I can always have an automation on state change.
of course. if there is an email, the state shall not be unknown. so can you verify that the unknown is *not* related to the above exception?

No, I do not get any failures to re-connect.
The sensor is always set to unknow 30s after the status update.
The emails stay in the inbox, they are not deleted, not even red. They just stay there, until I do a clean-up time to time (it is a dedicated inbox)

As a workaround, this seems to work:

````yaml
sensor:
  - platform: imap_email_content
    name: alarm_email
    server: imap.gmail.com
    port: 993
    username: !secret gmail_username
    password: !secret gmail_password
    senders:
      - !secret alarm_email
    value_template: "{{ subject.split('Alarm - ')[1] }}"
  - platform: template
    sensors: 
      alarm:
        friendly_name: Alarm
        value_template: >
          {% if is_state('sensor.alarm_email','unknown') %}
            {{ states('sensor.alarm') }}
          {% else %}
            {{ states('sensor.alarm_email') }}
          {% endif %}
````

But it does not mean the issue should not be solved.
I prepared something. How can we proceed to testing it with your setup?

I put in in custom_components and re-configured back to the original setup. 
Seems to be holding fine
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/44951610/82725866-558af980-9ce0-11ea-9cf9-2fc3d0eb4e17.png)
Thanks a lot for quick reaction.
Ok cool. I will open the PR soon. Thanks.

Hi

I did not exactly understand if the log is a real problem or just a log, because the software is just polling the server. I had asked you, but I only got a big logfile, not understanding, why it was necessary to paste it into the email. The first email contained the related lines anyway. 

The logline was added intentionally, it was a request from another maintainer.I also think they help understanding how imap state changes affect the sensor. 
The older version did not create a log when it was reconnecting. 
The lack of log does not mean that it was not reconnecting. 

A sensor will update its state always. This is the nature of sensors. 

In case of an empty mailbox, the sensor does not have enough information to hold its last retrieved message id in memory, because the last retrieved message id points to a non existing email. Reading from that email will lead to an exception. The log has been added there to see that there is an exception. In the old version there was no log at all.

Due to the exception in reading that email, it switches the sensor to unknown state. 
The reconnect is the default solution to any exception from the imap protocol. It is maybe possible to suppress reconnecting, however then its not unlikely that other users claim that there is a potential desync within the sensor imap connection state and the server imap state. So in this case I am unsure if the code can make everybody happy. A reconnect is a cleaner solution in my opinion. But you can make a PR with a different approach, if you like. I currently do not have enough time to work on this. In the second half of september maybe.

The workaround with an email in the mailbox works, because when the sensor updates its state, it *is* able to read the email with the last id it has in its internal sensor state. Then no exception is thrown, because it knows that the internal state matches server state. 

If the log is annoying, set its level to error or fatal, so that you do not see unnecessary logs. Currently it is INFO level, which is probably really unnecessary.
